Irrelevant

ih-REL-uh-vunt — stress the REL; if it's irrelevant, it's not relevant — it just doesn't matter here. · adjective

Hear It

What It Means

Irrelevant is not connected to the matter at hand; having no bearing on the topic.

The lawyer objected that the question was irrelevant to the case.

Worked Example

During a debate about the school lunch menu, a student stands up and describes his summer trip to the beach in loving detail. The room goes quiet. The moderator politely asks him to sit down.

His story has no bearing on the lunch-menu question — it is irrelevant. Unlike 'wrong,' an irrelevant point can be perfectly true; it just doesn't apply to the topic.

How Irrelevant Sits Among Its Neighbors

Synonyms — open each to see how it differs

unrelated

unrelated: having no connection to something

immaterial

immaterial: of no importance to the matter

beside the point

beside the point: not pertinent to the issue at hand

Antonyms

relevant

relevant: directly related to the matter

pertinent

pertinent: applying directly to the topic

How Strong Is It? — tangential → meaningless → irrelevant

tangential vs. irrelevant

tangential vs. irrelevant: Tangential is weaker than irrelevant — a tangential comment is at least loosely connected to the topic, while an irrelevant one has no connection at all.

meaningless vs. irrelevant

meaningless vs. irrelevant: Meaningless is stronger than irrelevant: an irrelevant fact simply doesn't apply here, but a meaningless one carries no significance in any context.

Sort It Out

Now place each word on the right side of irrelevant.

Build the Word

The pieces

prefix — ir- (in-)

prefix — ir- (in-): not (Latin)

root — lev-

root — lev-: to lift, to raise (Latin)

suffix — -ant

suffix — -ant: adjective-forming, 'doing' (Latin)

Put it together

Put it together: Latin relevare meant 'to lift up' — a relevant point 'bears upon' the matter, carrying weight in the discussion. Add ir- (not) and you get irrelevant: lifting nothing, carrying no weight on the topic.

Use the root in a new word: elevate

Use the root in a new word: elevate: The crane elevated the steel beam to the top floor.

Root Check

Word Choice

Irrelevant is used to set aside points that don't bear on the topic, usually with 'to' — 'irrelevant to the case,' 'irrelevant to the argument.'
